watchOS 27 will launch this fall as the next major update for Apple Watch, featuring a useful new capability that can improve your Apple Watch battery life: "Proactive Battery Extension Notifications."

watchOS 27 can proactively disable features you have never used to extend Apple Watch battery life.

watchOS 27 is about to launch, bringing two new apps to Apple Watch, a useful touch gesture, a brand-new default home screen, three health-related upgrades, and more.

Another new feature in watchOS 27 is designed to improve your Apple Watch battery life.

"Proactive Battery Extension Notifications" are a brand-new type of prompt you may see on your Apple Watch.

When you receive a battery extension notification, it means watchOS 27 has detected that you have several features you have never used, and disabling them can save battery power.

These features include various gestures, the "Raise to Speak" function that wakes Siri, and "Start Workout" reminders.

Each of these features involves background processing and places a certain burden on battery life.

Therefore, in watchOS 27, if the system detects that you have never used these features, it will automatically disable them. A "battery extension notification" will then be sent to inform you of the arrangement and give you the option to keep those features enabled.

If you use these features regularly, you will not see this notification. Of course, you can also manually disable these features in Settings at any time to get longer battery life.

Apple has not specified exactly how much extra battery life users can gain after disabling these features. But clearly, the power savings are significant enough to warrant building this brand-new battery extension feature.

Do you use Apple Watch features like "Raise to Speak," gestures, or "Start Workout" reminders? Will you keep them enabled going forward? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
